# sk Documentation

> The sk documentation set for LLMs: every public page grouped by audience, each with its title, link, and one-line summary.
> Full documentation in one file: llms-full.txt

## Start here

- [Bootstrap Preflight](BOOTSTRAP-PREFLIGHT.md): Version 1.0 — this text is byte-identical in every product of the family.
- [Start here](start-here.md): sk takes the work your team does the same way every week and runs it for you — reviewed before it goes live, permission-checked every time, and recorded so you can always show what happened.
- [Use cases](use-cases.md): What people actually run on sk — as cases, not features.

## Concepts

- [Concepts](concepts/README.md): Read this section and you can predict what sk will do before you run it — and say why, in the same words as everyone else on your team.
- [Connectors & Integration](concepts/connectors.md): Connect a system once, then use it from every workflow you ever write — and never let its secret touch a workflow definition, an AI prompt, or a log.
- [FAQ](concepts/faq.md): Short answers to the questions people ask in their first week, each pointing at the one page that covers it properly.
- [Concepts & Domain Model](concepts/glossary.md): One vocabulary, defined once.
- [Governance & Audit](concepts/governance-and-audit.md): Pass the audit on the first pass.
- [Knowledge & Skills](concepts/knowledge-and-skills.md): The AI proposes work the way your team does it, not the way a generic API tutorial does — because your conventions are in front of it while it writes.
- [Architecture Overview](concepts/overview.md): This page explains why sk's promise — describe it, approve it, it runs, and you can prove what it did — survives contact with production.
- [Reversibility & Trust Domains](concepts/reversibility-and-trust-domains.md): Give each piece of work the level of control it actually needs — no ceremony where mistakes are cheap, no blind spots where they are not.
- [When to use sk — and when not to](concepts/when-to-use.md): Most automation does not need sk, and saying so is the point of this page.
- [Why these primitives](concepts/why-these-primitives.md): A feature list says what a primitive does.
- [Workflow Execution](concepts/workflows.md): Once you approve a workflow, it takes the same path every time — no model reconsiders it on the next run.

## Operators

- [Operators](operators/README.md): Keep it running without babysitting it.
- [Chat Channels](operators/chat.md): Use sk from the chat your team already lives in.
- [Connectors & Credentials (operator guide)](operators/connectors-and-credentials.md): Connect a system once, reuse it everywhere — and the credential is never exposed.
- [Deploy & upgrade the engine](operators/deploy.md): Upgrading is a two-step operation you can do in the middle of the day: replace one file, restart one service.
- [Notifications](operators/notifications.md): Operators hear about what matters, not noise.
- [Observability & Resource Limits](operators/observability.md): See every run, understand content-free product usage, and catch drift before it costs you.
- [Quickstart — Operator](operators/quickstart.md): In 15 minutes your team has somewhere to put work that should run by itself — live, with a connected system to point at.
- [Runtime Dependencies](operators/runtime-dependencies.md): Discovery works against every documentation site, including the ones that render themselves in JavaScript — provided one thing is installed on the host.
- [Scheduling & Hooks (operator guide)](operators/scheduling-and-hooks.md): Work that runs when it should, whether or not anyone is watching — and nothing gets in without being checked at the door.
- [Drift-assisted repair in operations](operators/self-healing.md): When a vendor renames a field, moves an endpoint, or starts requiring a parameter, you get a repair to review — not a 3am page and a diagnosis from scratch.

## Authors

- [Authors](authors/README.md): Get from one sentence to a process that runs every week without you.
- [Ask your company's knowledge](authors/asking-your-knowledge.md): Ask a question where you already work, and the company answers from its own documents — naming what it read, or saying plainly that the answer isn't in there.
- [AI-Assisted Authoring](authors/authoring-workflows.md): Describe what should happen and have a reviewed, versioned workflow the same afternoon — instead of a build project that runs for weeks.
- [Choosing your surface](authors/choosing-your-surface.md): Do the work where it actually goes faster.
- [Use sk from a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, …)](authors/coding-agents.md): Every new session starts already knowing your domain's rules, looks your runbooks up instead of inventing them, and remembers what you taught it last time — once you have reviewed and approved that lesson.
- [Kontoverbindungen und Freigaben](authors/connections.md): Beides findest du im Cockpit unter Installation: die Kontoverbindungen im Abschnitt Kontoverbindungen der Seite Zugangsdaten, die vorbereiteten Änderungen oben auf Einstellungen.
- [Custom Skills](authors/custom-skills.md): Write down a convention once and stop repeating it.
- [Knowledge Sources](authors/knowledge-sources.md): Workflows follow your runbooks and policies instead of generic knowledge.
- [Model a Domain](authors/model-a-domain.md): Teach sk a whole field of work once, and every workflow in it arrives right the first time.
- [Quickstart — Authors](authors/quickstart.md): In about five minutes you will have described a piece of work in ordinary sentences and watched it run — no code written, nothing touched in a real system until you said so.
- [Using the `sk` REPL — authoring by conversation](authors/repl-tour.md): Go from idea to a governed, versioned workflow in minutes — no JSON, no glue code.

## Developers

- [Developers](developers/README.md): Run sk on your own infrastructure and change it safely.
- [Detailed Agent Navigation](developers/agent-navigation.md): This on-demand reference preserves the former root agent guide.
- [Bounded content publication](developers/bounded-content-publication.md): SubKit supports the documented ContentKit markdown revision and site release protocol as a finite repeated-run boundary.
- [Scheduled report decisions](developers/bounded-report-delivery.md): A saved draft, successful held preview and one-off send do not authorize future scheduled deliveries.
- [Bounded requests](developers/bounded-requests.md): A scheduled workflow runs without a person present, so a person approves its effects once, for a finite number of runs.
- [Capability matrix](developers/capabilities.md): Every answer here was read out of the code, not out of a feature list.
- [Coding-Agent Integration (Claude Code & Codex)](developers/coding-agent-integration.md): sk can act as the central knowledge and skill source for your coding agents.
- [Evidence process — verifying a behavioral / LLM-path change](developers/evidence-process.md): Changes to LLM-driven paths ship proven rather than guessed.
- [Input Surfaces](developers/input-surfaces.md): Meet your team where they already work—with one governed engine and one common MCP auth contract.
- [Quickstart — Developer](developers/quickstart.md): In about ten minutes you go from a clone to a passing test suite and an engine running on your machine — the setup you need before changing anything.
- [Recipe authoring](developers/recipes.md): Common automations start from a vetted blueprint, not a blank page.
- [Self-Host sk — Zero to Running](developers/self-host.md): sk runs inside your own infrastructure, so your data stays where it already is.
- [Step kinds — field reference](developers/step-kinds-reference.md): A Workflow is composed of Steps.
- [Machine tokens — swap an API key for a short-lived Bearer token](developers/token-exchange.md): An API key is a long-lived secret.
- [Tool palette and dispatch](developers/tool-palette.md): Every action an LLM can take against sk is a named tool that goes through one registry, one policy gate, and one audit trail.

## Admins

- [Admins — govern access](admins/README.md): Hand a team the keys without handing over the building.
- [Bootstrap Preflight](admins/bootstrap-preflight.md): Before a production engine migrates anything, it decides whether this release can run on the bootstrap it was given — and if it cannot, it exits 3 with one line and has changed nothing.
- [Configuring the engine](admins/configuration.md): SubKit keeps its canonical non-fundamental runtime configuration in PostgreSQL.
- [Credentials & Keys](admins/credentials-and-keys.md): Every integration secret is encrypted at rest, rotated on demand, and never logged, returned in an API response, or shown to the AI.
- [Production hardening — known caveats & TODOs](admins/production-hardening.md): Work through this page and you can go live knowing three things: every run is permission-checked and recorded, someone can answer an auditor's questions from what was written down, and you could rebuild the entire setup from a database backup alone.
- [Admin Quickstart](admins/quickstart.md): In about ten minutes your team can work on their own — signing in with the identity provider you already have, using credentials they never see, doing only what their role allows.
- [RBAC & Roles](admins/rbac-and-roles.md): Least-privilege by default, every decision auditable.

## Optional

- [subkit runtime settings](admins/settings-reference.md): Every value below lives in canonical runtime configuration and is editable via the Cockpit, HTTP/MCP settings APIs, sk settings configure, or sk settings set.
- [sk settings](authors/settings.md): Settings for the sk CLI itself — separate from the engine's runtime settings (see settings-reference).
- [Slash commands](authors/slash-commands.md): Slash commands run from the sk REPL.
- [Connector & recipe catalog](catalog.md): What ships in the box: 58 connector templates across 16 categories, carrying 240 recipes — pre-authored, runnable workflows you clone instead of starting from a blank page.
- [sk CLI reference](developers/cli-reference.md): Every sk command and argument — and the surface authoring runs through: creating or changing a workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill is a definition edit, and definition edits belong here, where the change is a file you can read and a command you can re-run.
